column1: # THE COHERENT PROSPECTIVE 2-6 SITE BUNDLES CONSIDERED.
# A candidate is a NAMED, COHERENT group of sites related by a shared
# semantic invariant / operator family, not by proximity in the source.
# Every candidate that was considered is listed here, including the
# ones that will be excluded, so that the exclusion ledger is complete
# The candidate identity is stable and deterministic: the family name
# plus the member set. Two candidates never share a member set.

column5: X86_64_COMPARISON_CONDITION_CODE_AND_BOOLEAN_MATERIALISATION: one IrCmpKind maps to exactly one machine condition-code suffix and one inverse suffix, and the same mapping decides the SETcc materialisation
column6: W-X86-CC-LT (a<b emits jl); W-X86-CC-LE (a<=b emits jle); W-X86-CC-GT (a>b emits jg); W-X86-CC-EQ (a==b emits je); W-X86-CC-NE (a!=b emits jne); W-X86-CC-INV (the false-side suffix); W-X86-SETCC (a comparison assigned to a variable emits set<cc> plus movzbq)

column5: AARCH64_COMPARISON_CONDITION_CODE_AND_BOOLEAN_MATERIALISATION: the same IrCmpKind family maps to one AArch64 condition suffix, its inverse, and the cset materialisation
column6: W-A64-CC-LT (a<b emits b.lt); W-A64-CC-LE (a<=b emits b.le); W-A64-CC-GT (a>b emits b.gt); W-A64-CC-EQ (a==b emits b.eq); W-A64-CC-NE (a!=b emits b.ne); W-A64-CC-INV (the false-side suffix); W-A64-CSET (a comparison assigned to a variable emits cset)

column5: TARGET_AGNOSTIC_COMPARISON_CONDITION_CODE_FAMILY: one IrCmpKind-to-condition-code decision, expressed once per backend, with the two backends' tables as parallel instances of one invariant
column6: as CAND-CMP-CC-X86 and CAND-CMP-CC-A64, per backend

column5: IR_VALUE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION: the IrValueType domain partitions into float and integer classes, and every backend and lowering step asks that partition
column6: W-IR-FLOAT-ISFLOAT (a float value reaches the float path); W-IR-INT-ISINT (an integer value reaches the integer path)

column5: IR_TYPE_PROJECTION: the AST type domain projects onto the IR value-type domain, and the IR opcode domain is classified into comparison opcodes
column6: W-IR-CONVERT (an int, char, float or pointer AST type projects to the matching IR value type); W-IR-OPISCMP (an IR_ICMP opcode is recognised as a comparison)

column5: IR_TYPE_ANALYSIS_FAMILY: the type-classification and type-projection decisions that every lowering and backend step consults
